description: The VALIDATE statement (ISO §2023:14.9.50) - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:IV.6.4.2.3.1 lists 'The imperative verbs are:' ACCEPT through WRITE with no VALIDATE among them, and VALIDATE is not in the §1985:IV.8 list ('The following is a list of COBOL reserved words for the seven required modules and the five optional modules'), whose V entries are VALUE, VALUES and VARYING; §2002:14.8.46 has the statement ('The VALIDATE statement invokes data validation, input distribution, and error indication for a data item'), §2002:F.1 item 6 lists VALIDATE among 'The following reserved words have been added', and §2002:F.2 item 143 states the change: 'Validate facility. The new statement VALIDATE was added, giving the ability to perform comprehensive data validation.' §2014:14.9.46 keeps the statement, so 2014 = 2023 (§2023:14.9.50.1 the same sentence; 2023 marks the facility obsolete, VCR row 95). The facility is declined (Annex A.4.14; docs/CONFORMANCE.md §4 item 3): from 2002 the statement is accepted inert under COBOL1580. The grammar arm is the UNION grammar, predicated only on the verb's spelling, and the VersionConformancePass parse arm (VisitValidateFacilityStatement) names the edition on RECOGNITION, so a VALIDATE statement at --std 85 answers COBOL0900 (kb/Work PB3148: a reservation predicate had made it a bare parse error at its operand). A COBOL-85 program that declares a data item VALIDATE keeps it: the reservation gate retypes every occurrence of the declared word to a user-defined word (kb/Work PB655).
